sections.h2: Is it better to list or sell as-is in Irondequoit?
sections.html:
It comes down to the house's condition and your calendar. Irondequoit is a Rochester suburb that grew fast after World War II, so the roof, the furnace and the basement often decide which route pays more.

Homes here are lived in by their owners at a rate of 78.8%, and the midpoint value is $182,500, so one large repair can take a real bite out of a sale. Get a contractor quote or two before listing. Modest work favors a regular listing. Heavy work, a vacant or inherited house, or back taxes can favor an as-is sale that stops the carrying costs.

  • Agent listing: the widest audience, with commission, showings and lender approval attached.
  • Owner sale: you keep the commission and run the marketing, haggling and paperwork.
  • As-is cash sale: fewer contingencies and a date you can often pick, usually at a lower price.

Put every bid in writing with the price, closing date, proof of funds and closing costs, then compare what each would leave you.

sections.h2: Where is Irondequoit and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Irondequoit sits in north-central Monroe County between the Genesee River on the west and Irondequoit Bay on the east, with the Lake Ontario shoreline on the north. Water borders it on three sides, which makes it a headland. The City of Rochester lies south and west, and Penfield, Webster and Brighton touch it on the east and southeast.

The boundary with Rochester is odd. A thin strip of city land runs north along the east bank of the Genesee, and the northern half of Durand Eastman Park, along with Seneca Park, belongs to the city, not the town. If your address says Irondequoit but you are close to those parks, check the tax bill to see which municipality actually taxes the house.

The town was set off from Brighton in 1839. In the late 1800s its lakefront was a tourist area for Rochester residents, once called the Coney Island of Western New York. After World War II the population climbed from 23,376 in 1940 to 55,337 in 1960 as returning veterans looked for homes. The West Irondequoit and East Irondequoit central school districts serve the town, and its colonial-style Town Hall dates to 1951.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Irondequoit homeowners?
sections.html:
About 50,200 people live in the town, 1.7% fewer than at the 2020 base. Residents 65 and over make up 22.6% of the town, and estates are one reason such houses reach the market.

sections.h2: When are Irondequoit property taxes due?
sections.html:
The town's Tax Office, run by the Receiver of Taxes, takes in Town, County and School tax. Two bills arrive each year: the Town and County bill goes out at the end of December with a February 10 deadline, and the School bill goes out at the end of August with an October 1 deadline.

A deadline that lands on a closed day moves to the next business day. Under state law a bill that never arrived still leaves the tax owed, and the office states that it cannot waive penalties. If a non-escrow owner has not received a bill within a week of mailing, the Tax Office at 585-336-6050 will send a copy, and the Monroe County website shows bills too.

To look up a parcel, use Monroe County's Real Property Portal: agree to the disclaimer, enter the house number and street, then open the Pay Property Taxes icon to view school and combined town and county statements and the payment history. Print the current statements for your closing attorney.

sections.h2: What are the key assessment dates for Irondequoit owners?
sections.html:
The town publishes a calendar of eight dates that shape every owner's bill. A sale does not pause any of them, so they are worth knowing when you time a listing.

  • March 1: taxable status date and last day for new and renewal exemption applications.
  • May 1: tentative roll becomes public, with a paper copy at Town Hall.
  • Third Tuesday in May: school budget vote.
  • Fourth Tuesday in May: Grievance Day.
  • July 1: final roll and valuation date. A judicial review (SCAR hearing) can be requested within 30 days after the final roll date.
  • Early September and early January: school and Town and County bills are mailed.

The final roll drives the next school bill and the next Town and County bill, so a buyer closing in summer inherits whatever figure appears on it. Read it before you settle on a price.

sections.h2: How does a grievance work in Irondequoit?
sections.html:
Applications go to the Assessor's Office from May 1 until Grievance Day. The 2026 hearing took place on May 26, and counting the fourth Tuesday puts the next one on May 25, 2027. This town-level step comes first, and a small claims review is open only to owners who have completed it.

The town asks for one original of Form RP-524 plus four copies, with supporting documents for each board member. Anyone who wants a hearing needs an appointment, and in 2026 that paperwork was due one week ahead. The assessor's tentative figure is presumed correct, so you carry the burden of proof. Credible evidence includes a recent appraisal, a purchase contract, a list of recent sales of similar homes or a broker's written opinion of value. Tax information is not accepted as evidence of value.

Before the hearing the assessor may offer a stipulation, which you can take or leave; taking it fixes the assessed value at the agreed figure. If the board's decision disappoints you, a Small Claims Assessment Review in Monroe County Supreme Court is available for $30 under Section 730 of the Real Property Tax Law. The town also ran informal review appointments in March and April of 2026 and publishes a comparable sales book built from sales dated 7/1/2024 to 7/1/2025.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies in Irondequoit, and who files the deed?
sections.html:
Sellers owe the state $2 for each $500 of price unless the contract moves the cost. At the town's midpoint home value of $182,500 that comes to $730, from 365 units of $500.

Form TP-584 reports it. A residential price of $1 million or more adds a 1% charge for the buyer.

Irondequoit deeds are filed at the Monroe County Clerk's Office downtown, 39 W. Main Street, Room 101, Rochester, NY 14614. Closing lawyers and title companies normally make the trip for you.

sections.h2: What goes on my checklist before I say yes to a direct buyer?
sections.html:
Add up everything you keep after costs, and then consider the calendar. A bigger listing price can lose its lead to commission, repairs and months of mortgage, tax and utility payments.

  • Have the buyer state in writing who covers the transfer tax and closing costs.
  • Ask for proof of funds and a fixed closing day.
  • Print your Monroe County portal statements so any unpaid tax is cleared at closing.
  • Get a listing-price opinion from a local agent as a yardstick.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Irondequoit?
faqs.a: The fourth Tuesday of May, so May 25, 2027 is the next. Applications can be filed from May 1 up to that day, and a hearing requires an appointment.

faqs.q: When are Irondequoit property taxes due?
faqs.a: The Town and County bill is due February 10 and the School bill October 1. A deadline on a closed day rolls to the next business day with no penalty.

faqs.q: How much does a small claims assessment review cost in Irondequoit?
faqs.a: It costs $30 under Section 730 of the Real Property Tax Law, and Monroe County Supreme Court handles it. The town grievance has to come first.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when an Irondequoit house sells?
faqs.a: The seller, at $2 per $500, unless the contract says the buyer takes it on. The buyer owes the extra 1% on residential sales of $1 million or more.

faqs.q: Is Seneca Park part of Irondequoit?
faqs.a: No. Seneca Park and the northern half of Durand Eastman Park are in the City of Rochester, though they lie along the town's western and northern edges. A house close to them deserves a look at its tax bill.
